body: Tarot is a set of 78 cards with pictures on them.
There are two groups: 22 cards called the Major Arcana, and 56 called the Minor Arcana. You do not need to memorize the names now.
In DECIDE., cards are used as hints for thinking.
For example, if you are wondering 'Should I message a friend?', you draw one card and read its explanation.
Reading it, you might think 'A short message feels doable,' or 'Maybe not today.'
Either way, it becomes a chance to notice your own feelings.
You can read each card's meaning right there, on the spot. There is no need to memorize all of them.
In the end, what to do is your own choice.
points: There are 78 cards in total. You can read the meaning after you draw
Think with the card as a hint, and decide for yourself

choices: Just read it after you draw
quiz.explain: The meaning appears on screen. Start by reading the words that catch your eye.
quiz.q: Do you have to memorize every card's meaning to use tarot?

lessons.summary: A tool for thinking about your own feelings, through the pictures and words on the cards.
lessons.title: What is tarot?

body: The Major Arcana are 22 cards, from number 0, 'The Fool,' to number 21, 'The World.'
They represent things like the feeling of starting something new, or time spent pausing to think.

For example, 'The Fool' is a hint for trying something new in a small way. 'Strength' is a hint for facing things calmly rather than forcing them. 'The World' is a hint for marking what you have completed so far.
There is also a way of remembering the 22 cards as a story of one person having many experiences.
It is called 'The Fool's Journey.' The divisions below are one way of reading that story.
The card you draw does not decide what stage of life you are in.
Try thinking about which parts feel similar to where you are now.
points: The Major Arcana are 22 cards, numbered 0 to 21
The story is a memory aid. You do not need to memorize it all

quiz.explain: Number 21 is 'The World.' It can be read as finishing one thing.
quiz.q: What is the name of card number 21?

lessons.summary: 22 cards for thinking about 'beginning,' 'being torn,' 'finishing,' and more.
lessons.title: What are the Major Arcana?

body: The Minor Arcana are 56 cards.
There are four groups — Wands, Cups, Swords, and Pentacles — with 14 cards each.
You can tell the four groups apart by the tools drawn on them. The picture below shows the first card (the Ace) of each.
For example, with Wands, ask 'What do I want to try?' With Cups, ask 'How do I — and how do they — feel?'
It gives you a chance to look at what you are deciding from a different direction than usual.
Fire, Water, Air, and Earth are images attached to each group.
If it feels difficult, it is fine to start by reading just the picture and everyday words.
points: Wands = action, Cups = feelings, Swords = thinking, Pentacles = daily life
Use the picture and group as hints to think about what you are deciding now

quiz.explain: Pentacles show coins, and give hints for thinking about daily life and money.
quiz.q: Which group is for thinking about money and daily life?

lessons.summary: Look at them through four lenses: motivation, feelings, thinking, and daily life.
lessons.title: The four groups of the Minor Arcana

body: The Minor Arcana have number cards from 1 to 10, and four kinds of court cards.
The number 1 is called the 'Ace.'
Numbers are guides for remembering meanings. For example, 1 is a beginning, 5 is a scene of clashing or worrying, and 10 is a point of completion.
However, the explanation differs from card to card, even for the same number.
The court cards are four kinds: Page, Knight, Queen, and King.
A Page can be read as someone beginning to learn, a Knight as someone who acts, a Queen as someone who stays close to others, and a King as someone who supports others through experience.
For example, the 'Eight of Pentacles' shows coins being finished one by one.
From that, you can think of the meaning 'practice little by little.' Do not decide by the number table alone — look at the picture and the explanation too.
points: Numbers and people are guides. Read each card's own explanation too
Court cards do not determine anyone's actual age or gender

choices: Look at the picture and each card's explanation too
quiz.explain: Numbers are guides. Reading the picture and explanation together shows you how each card differs.
quiz.q: Can you decide a card's meaning by its number alone?

lessons.summary: Numbers and people are guides to help you remember the meanings.
lessons.title: Looking at number and court cards

body: A card drawn in its normal orientation is called 'upright,' and a card drawn upside down is called 'reversed.'
Either way, the explanation appears on screen.
Reversed does not mean a bad result is guaranteed.
It can be read as a hint for reviewing: 'Am I overdoing it?' or 'Maybe I can rest a little.'
For example, 'The Star' reversed has a meaning like hope being hard to see.
Rather than being afraid, you can use it as a chance to think: 'Is my goal too big?' or 'Maybe I will rest today.'
To compare meanings, open a card in the collection and tap 'Upright' or 'Reversed.'
In the 'Simple' setting, you can use upright cards only.
points: Upright is the normal orientation. Reversed is upside down
Reversed is also a hint for thinking about your situation

choices: Something bad is guaranteed to happen
Read it as a hint for reviewing
You must not read the explanation
quiz.explain: Even reversed, your future is not decided. From the explanation, think about what to watch out for now.

lessons.summary: Upside down does not mean 'something bad will happen.'
lessons.title: What if a card comes out upside down?

body: First, think of one thing you want to decide. For example, 'Should I message a friend?'
Use a one-card draw to decide one thing, and a two-card draw to compare two candidates.
When you draw a card, read its explanation.
Notice how you felt: 'I want to message them,' or 'I want to stop for now.' You do not need to guess the 'right answer.'
Press 'DECIDE.' on the result to choose what to do. In a one-card draw, there are 'Go ahead,' 'Pass,' and 'Hold.'
'Pass' means not doing it this time, and 'Hold' means deciding later.
You can keep what you decided with 'Record this decision.' The one-line memo can be left blank.
Later, open 'Log' at the bottom and leave how it went — it becomes a hint for the next time you decide.
To read more about a card's meaning, tap its picture or name.
You can also practice from 'How to use' on the first screen.
points: Read the card's explanation first, then choose for yourself
You can read back what you decided from 'Log'

quiz.explain: The card is a hint for thinking. Check your own feelings now, too, and choose for yourself.
quiz.q: Who decides what to do in the end?

lessons.summary: Use it in this order: picture it → draw → choose for yourself → read it back later.
lessons.title: Try using DECIDE. once
